newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares rise on outside buying.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares rise on outside buying.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange rose on Sunday in trade dominated by deals on heavyweight firms reported to be the focus of foreign interest, dealers said.

Arab International Hotels, which owns the five-star Marriott, was the focus of a 277,142-dinar deal by one investor, making it by far the busiest traded stock in an otherwise thin market. It rose 0.10 dinars to 4.60 dinars.
Jordan Phosphate Mines, a leading exporter which reported a healthy rise in 1996 revenues last week, maintained its strong turnover for the second day running, but stood unchanged at 3.40 dinars.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.15 points to 154.04 points in moderate turnover of 657,174 dinars ($928,211).
Blue-chip Arab Bank, the third busiest stock, shed 0.25 dinars to 256.000 dinars in trade worth 51,200 dinars.

"What improved the market was outside buying with some interest on stock such as Jordan Phosphates and Jordan Petroleum Refinery," said Husam al-Hanbali, a broker who heads Jordan's Arab Banking Corporation's brokerage arm.

Jordan Petroleum Refinery was among the handful of firms that did well on Sunday. The stock which had risen steadily since Jordan's agreement last week for cheap Iraqi oil throughout 1997, rose 0.06 dinars to 10.01 dinars in trade worth nearly 32,396 dinars.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.17 percent to 81.92 points.
